title: 12 Boys Trapped in a Flooded Cave. Then a Light Came Up #shorts
description:
Case 020. On 23 June 2018 twelve boys from a junior football team and their coach walked into the Tham Luang cave in Chiang Rai province, northern Thailand. Heavy rain flooded the passages behind them; their bicycles were found at the entrance that evening. Driven deeper by the rising water, the thirteen ended up on a slope of mud far inside the cave, in the dark, while outside a search grew to thousands of people and divers fought the flooded passages. On 2 July, after nine nights, the British cave divers Rick Stanton and John Volanthen surfaced in a chamber and found all thirteen alive. Getting them out was the harder part: the way out lay underwater, through tight, twisting flooded tunnels with a strong current. On 6 July a Thai rescuer, the former navy diver Saman Kunan, died while placing air tanks in the cave. Between 8 and 10 July the boys and their coach were sedated, fitted with full-face masks and carried out underwater by divers, one at a time, and all thirteen came out alive. A few hours after the last of them was out, the pumping failed and the water rose again. Rook didn't believe it either.

Animated reconstruction of a true story. The cave mouth, the passages, the chamber and the flooded tunnel in the film are generic low-poly sets, not a survey of the real cave; the thirteen, the divers and the rescuers are simple figures and nobody's likeness is attempted; shirts, gear and helmets are plain and carry no badge or brand. The cross-section card is a diagram of the idea, not a map, and shows no distances, because sources differ on how far inside the group was found. The film does not show how the rescuer died: a lamp dims and Rook takes his hat off. Staging details such as the torches, the brass torch Rook keeps, the tally marks and the work light are reconstruction, not record.

experiments.E1_E2: spine v2: Rook doubts the story standing on a boulder in the flooded passage, the water racing past in the same shot, in one line of 1.1 s (5.7 s to 6.8 s); no office, no cutaway. The story then runs forward from the hook; date and place appear only as on-screen labels (23 JUNE 2018, THAM LUANG, THAILAND, 2 JULY 2018, 8-10 JULY 2018). The only name narrated is Saman Kunan's, at the beat that is about him.
experiments.E3: batch Short 2 (even): wide first frame - the cave mouth in the rain with the bicycles in the foreground. This follows the brief; the production checklist's 'first shot shows the subject close' is met by the bicycles and the three figures on the path rather than by a face.
experiments.E4: 'Case closed.' ending (the brief's choice for this case: a rescuer died, so no question is put to viewers).
experiments.E7: hook_text is set (TRAPPED IN A / FLOODED CAVE). AUTHORING.md makes it mandatory for every episode while the experiment log wants half the batch without it; the mandatory rule was followed. Short 1 (r016) has none, so the two can still be compared.
experiments.E8: tail 0.4 s; the last line ('And it began the day') runs into the first ('Twelve boys and their coach walk into a cave'), and the last shot is the opening shot played back to its first frame, lightning included.
experiments.rook_action: He counts the thirteen along the ledge with a wingtip (shot 18) and sounds the water with a weighted line that finds no bottom (shots 22 and 23). Mannerisms: beak tap (shot 7), hat jump and shed feather (shot 23), hat to chest (shot 25), pocketing the shiny thing and the brim pulled down (shot 37).

sound_plan.first_frame: One 'hit' at 0.03 s with the lightning flash that lights the first frame (the gate needs an impact in the first second; here it is the thunderclap, a story sound), thunder rolling from 0.1 s over rain.
sound_plan.hook: Rain throughout; a wave and a splash as the water comes in over the lip; splashes and a shout as the arch goes under.
sound_plan.music: The engine's score follows the segment moods: hook, tense for Rook's line, action for the flight, tense for the wait, wonder for the light, tense for the re-hook, sad for Saman Kunan (the sad mood carries no drum loop), tense for the dive out, triumph, calm, end. The engine cannot delay the music's entry, so 'music enters once the story moves' is approximated by the sparse hook mood.
sound_plan.hush: Shot 30 (the squeeze): the music drops out for the breath before 'all thirteen come out alive'.
sound_plan.voice: Narration is ducked over the bed by the engine; measured in the local rehearsal (see quality_gate).

source_notes: Read for this run (fetched 16 Nov 2026): Wikipedia 'Tham Luang cave rescue' (first part of the article read in full; later sections only in summary and not relied on); Reuters, 'Timeline: Thai cave rescue that transfixed the world for 17 days' (24 June 2019, read on Yahoo News); ITV News, 'How the Thailand cave ordeal unfolded' (10 July 2018); ABC News / Good Morning America, 'With all odds against them, how rescuers pulled off miracle Thai cave mission' (12 July 2018); Shepton Mallet Caving Club, 'A summary of the Tham Luang Rescue' (a caver's day-by-day timeline); CNN Newsource via ABC15, 'Boys rescued from cave in Thailand were sedated with ketamine' (4 April 2019, reporting the rescuers' letter in the New England Journal of Medicine); The New Daily (6 April 2019) on the same letter. Pages that could not be read: BBC, The Guardian, Reuters' own site, AP, NPR, CNN's own site, Britannica, National Geographic, Smithsonian, ABC Australia, History, SBS, the British Cave Rescue Council and the Australian of the Year page (blocked, refused or errors). Every narrated fact is in at least two of the pages read. Twelve boys and their coach went into the cave on 23 June 2018: Wikipedia, Reuters, ITV, ABC News. Rain flooded the cave and trapped them: Wikipedia ('stranded in the tunnels by sudden and continuous rainfall'), Reuters ('rising flood water after heavy rain would soon trap them'), ITV. Bicycles at the entrance: Wikipedia ('abandoned bicycles and bags near the entrance'), ITV ('bikes are found parked and locked at the cave entrance'), ABC News, Shepton. Driven deeper by the water onto a slope of mud: Wikipedia (they fled rising water; found on 'a narrow rock shelf', also called an 'elevated rock'), Reuters ('on a muddy slope'), ABC News ('a small beach'); the film uses the muddy slope. Nine nights: Reuters ('nine nights inside the cave complex'), Wikipedia (found nine days after entering); ABC News counts 'ten days after the group went missing', which is the same span counted inclusively. Divers working against the flood meanwhile: ITV ('flooding underground passages faster than water can be pumped out'), Reuters, Shepton. Found on 2 July by the British divers Rick Stanton and John Volanthen, all thirteen alive: all five timeline sources. The way out was through flooded passages and some of the boys could not swim: Wikipedia ('It was believed that some of the group could not swim'; teaching them to dive was judged too risky), ABC News ('most of them did not know how to swim'); the film says 'some', which both support. Saman Kunan, a former Thai navy diver, died on 6 July while placing air tanks: Wikipedia, Reuters, ABC News ('delivering extra air tanks'), ITV (unnamed), Shepton ('to stage cylinders'). Sedated, in full-face masks, carried out by divers one at a time: Wikipedia (ketamine given by the anaesthetist Richard Harris; 'positive pressure full-face mask'), CNN Newsource ('given unspecified doses of ketamine', 'full-face masks supplying oxygen', 'while we were carrying them out'), The New Daily, ABC News ('normally one diver per boy'). Out over three days, 8 to 10 July, four, four and five: Wikipedia, Reuters, ITV, ABC News. Hours after the last of them was out the pumping failed and the water rose: ABC News ('Just two hours after the last rescue was made ... the pumps ... broke down'), Shepton (at 21:10, after the last boy reached the entrance at 18:53, 'a water pipe coupling breaks causing the water to rise rapidly'), Wikipedia ('a water pipe burst and the main pump stopped working'). Conflicts and things kept out of the film. Distance: Wikipedia's lead says about 2 km from the entrance, ABC News 2.9 miles, Shepton about 4 km plus 750 m, so no distance is narrated or drawn and the cross-section card says NOT TO SCALE. What they sat on: rock shelf, muddy slope or small beach, see above. Kunan's age and rank differ between pages (37 or 38; petty officer, later promoted), so neither is given. The cause of the water rising at the end is a failed pump in two sources and a broken pipe coupling in the third; the narration says 'the pumps fail', which two support, and the description says 'the pumping failed'. The exchange usually quoted from the divers' video ('How many of you?' 'Thirteen.' 'Brilliant.') was found verbatim in only one page read, so it is not quoted: Rook counts instead. 'Almost no food' and the coach leading meditation were each confirmed in only one page read and were cut from the script. Whether the boys were fully unconscious differs (Wikipedia 'fully unconscious'; the journal reports say sedated), so the film says 'sedate'. The first script draft said 'the only way out is underwater' and 'the cave floods again'; both were softened to 'the way out is underwater' and 'the water rises again' because drilling and waiting were also considered and the sources describe water rising in the inner chambers, not the whole cave. Left out for length: the thousands of volunteers and soldiers, the pumping operation and the water diverted on the mountain, the falling oxygen in the chamber, the navy divers and the army doctor who stayed with the group, the order in which the boys came out (disputed), the boys' ages and names, and the later lives of those involved. Staging choices that are not facts: the number of bicycles (five are shown), the boys' torches and the torch that goes out, the low arch and the boulder, the tally marks, the silver blanket, the stretcher under a foil blanket, the work lights, the small brass torch Rook keeps, the colours of shirts and helmets, and the time of day of each scene. Second check, by the run that took this case over after the first run was cut off (16 Nov 2026): four more pages were read against the script, namely HISTORY.com 'Last of Thai soccer team rescued from cave' (10 July entry), NPR 'Pump Fails At Thai Cave Hours After Soccer Boys Rescued' (11 July 2018), the Telegraph report carried by Yahoo News 'Thailand cave rescue: Water pumps failed just after last boy escaped' and the South China Morning Post's account of the divers' interviews. They confirm: entry on 23 June and the monsoon flood (HISTORY, NPR); found alive on 2 July by two British divers after a nine-day search (HISTORY; NPR and the Telegraph give the date); the escape was underwater through 'dangerous, tight and twisting passageways, with strong currents' (HISTORY) and 'twisting, jagged submerged corridors in swirling murky waters' (Telegraph); Saman Kunan, a former Thai navy SEAL, died on 6 July delivering air tanks (HISTORY, Telegraph); the boys were sedated and wore full-face masks (HISTORY); out on 8, 9 and 10 July, all thirteen alive (HISTORY, NPR, SCMP); the main pump failed about three hours (NPR), 'a few hours' (Telegraph), 'just hours' (SCMP) after the last of them was out, while rescue workers were still inside; all of those got out. Changed because of this check: the line 'some of these boys can't even swim' was cut. The first run had it from Wikipedia ('it was believed that some of the group could not swim') and ABC News ('most'), but none of the four pages read in the second check states it, and it was reported after the rescue that the coach said all of the boys could swim; a disputed claim is not narrated as fact. The line now says the way out is 'through tight, twisting tunnels in a strong current', which HISTORY and the Telegraph both support, and the label on those shots reads UNDERWATER. The description no longer calls the coach an assistant coach because only some pages do. 'Nine nights' counts 23 June to 2 July, the time until they were found (Reuters, and HISTORY's nine-day search); it is not the whole time in the cave, which was 17 or 18 days depending on the page. 'One by one' means each boy was dived out individually with his own diver, four on each of the first two days and five on the last; it does not mean one a day. The boy who pulls his foot back from the water is staging, not record.

quality_gate.method: Two runs. The first run (cut off before shipping) built the script, storyboard and world and went through three contact-sheet rounds. The run that took the case over reviewed it again from scratch in five rounds. Round 1: low-res contact sheet of all 35 3D shots plus preview stills of every 3D kind at 15% and 85% of the shot (70 stills). Found: two black bars lying on the ground in the morning shots (the close-up hand props had been left at the world origin, inside the cave-mouth set); black shards in the puddles; the glow under the water was a flat white disc; Rook had his back to the camera for the whole count; Rook's face was black beside the pump and cropped off the left edge at the stretcher; he was small in the 'I was wrong' shot. Round 2 (16 preview stills of the changed shots): the hands are parked out of sight, Rook walks along the row in three-quarter view pointing at the boys and turns to camera on thirteen, the glow is a soft teal pool, Rook flies level with the stretcher inside the frame, a lamp lights his face at the pump; the count's last frames had the camera inside a boulder, and one black wedge was still in a puddle. Round 3 (14 stills, one at 720x1280): the camera path was corrected; the wedge was two puddles overlapping in the same plane, which Cycles renders black, so each puddle now sits at its own height. Round 4: second full contact sheet, clean. Round 5: a full-length rehearsal (216x384, 4 samples, 12 fps, all 518 3D frames) composited with captions, labels, overlays, inserts and sound, looked at as one composited still per shot and as a 4-frames-per-second sheet of the whole video (182 frames), plus six frames pulled at larger size (first frame, last frame, the three cards, the case board). Found: the new label on shots 22 and 23 was too long for its slide-in and was shortened to UNDERWATER; the second line of the hook text touched both edges of the frame and was re-broken as TRAPPED IN A / FLOODED CAVE. The final rehearsal passed the automated gate locally: 39 shots, mean 1.17 s, longest 1.62 s, Rook acting in 16 of 39 shots (41%), -14.6 LUFS, peak -1.3 dBFS, voice 11.2 dB over the bed, closest match to any earlier episode 0.67 (shot 17 against r016-simpson; the limit is 0.93). Duration 45.5 s. The cloud render runs the real gate at 720x1280 and 60 fps.
quality_gate.checked: Every 3D kind in the storyboard exists in world3d.SHOTS3D (checked by script); HOST lists the 16 kinds in which Rook is placed; mouth_wide is the only kind used twice (first and last shot, for the loop). The doubt line is 1.03 s and is spoken on the boulder with the water racing past. The re-hook starts at 19.9 s of 45.5 s (44%). One hush shot (31, the squeeze). Tail 0.4 s; the last shot returns to the opening framing and the last line runs into the first. Dates and names on screen (23 JUNE 2018, THAM LUANG, THAILAND, 2 JULY 2018, SAMAN KUNAN, 8-10 JULY 2018, NINE NIGHTS, 13 OF 13) were checked against the sources. Nothing graphic is shown; the rescuer's death is a lamp dimming and Rook with his hat off, and Rook makes no joke from that beat on. No badge, brand, flag or likeness appears.
quality_gate.not_met: Loudness range measures 1.7 LU (ffmpeg ebur128) against the checklist's 4 LU. This is the engine's mix, not this episode: the published Case 016 Short measures the same 1.7 LU on its review copy. The audio was measured, not listened to. Full-resolution preview of every shot at two points was done at 360x640, with one shot at 720x1280; the cloud render is the first full-resolution pass.
